subject: history_social
passage: The Chausath Yogini temple at Mitaoli, in the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh, stands on a low hill and is built as a ring: sixty-four small chambers open inward onto a circular courtyard, at the center of which a separate shrine stands under the open sky. An inscription dates the temple to the fourteenth century, and the chambers once housed the sixty-four goddesses ______ images gave the temple its name. Nearly all of those images have since disappeared, so historians rely on better-preserved yogini temples elsewhere in India to imagine how this one originally looked.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The blank must connect "the sixty-four goddesses" to the clause "images gave the temple its name" and show that the images belonged to the goddesses. Only the relative possessive pronoun "whose" does both jobs: "the goddesses whose images gave the temple its name."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Their" is a possessive, but it is not a relative pronoun, so it leaves two clauses run together with nothing joining them.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Whom" is an object pronoun and cannot show that the images belonged to the goddesses.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Which" cannot show possession; "the goddesses which images" does not make sense.
explanation.D: Correct. The relative pronoun "whose" links the clause to "goddesses" and shows that the images were theirs.
